_comment: Official-document evidence for tool rules. file = FRET repository docs (NASA-SW-VnV/fret, commit cf0f913, fret-electron/docs/_media/user-interface/examples). 'documents' says what the quote establishes: CONSTRUCT = the FRETish construct exists and what it means; it never says WHICH construct fits a given natural language sentence. A rule that picks one documented alternative for a template phrase stays a CHOICE and is listed as unsourced in ownership.md.

R-EARS-WHEN.quote: A regular condition is introduced by the keyword upon (or when, where, if).
R-EARS-WHEN.documents: CONSTRUCT; upon, when, if, where give the same requirement by the official parser (S1a), so the keyword choice among them is immaterial

R-SP-BEFORE.quote: Before taxiing & receivedClearance the plane shall always satisfy !takeoff

R-SP-AFTER.quote: After landed & powerOff the doors shall within 3 seconds satisfy unlocked

R-TIME-UNTIL.quote: The timing until means that the response must hold at least until strictly before the STOP_Condition holds.

R-TIME-BEFORE.quote: The timing before means that the response must happen at least once strictly before the STOP_CONDITION holds.

R-TIME-NEXT.quote: When currentOverload the circuitBreaker shall, at the next timepoint, satisfy shutoff

R-TIME-WITHIN.quote: In landing mode, the the system shall within 2 seconds satisfy is_stable

R-TIME-FOR.quote: When errorCondition, the system shall, for 4 seconds, satisfy alarmOn

R-TIME-AFTER.quote: When input = 1, the integrator shall, after 10 ticks, satisfy output=10

R-SP-UNIV.quote: The autopilot shall always satisfy if allGood then state = nominal

R-SP-ABS.quote: In drivingMode the system shall never satisfy cellPhoneOn & !cellPhoneHandsFree

R-SP-EXIST.quote: In landingMode the system shall eventually satisfy LandingGearLowered

R-NEG.quote: In drivingMode the system shall never satisfy cellPhoneOn & !cellPhoneHandsFree

R2-TM-SLOT.quote: immediately, initially, at the first timepoint, at the same timepoint (synonyms)

R-MULTI.quote: The condition can be a sequence of Boolean expressions, optionally connected by the keywords and and or.

R-ADV-HY.quote: The keyword While for boolean expressions has a meaning like In for mode variables.

R-BP-SUFFIX.quote: In landing mode, the the system shall within 2 seconds satisfy is_stable

R-BP-UNLESS.quote: A regular condition is introduced by the keyword upon (or when, where, if).
R-BP-UNLESS.documents: CONSTRUCT; `unless p` is `if !(p)` by the official parser (S2)

R-MAS-ABLE.quote: The current version of FRET supports the form: satisfy BEXP (Boolean Expression, see the help for the Condition field).
R-MAS-ABLE.documents: FORCED BY THE TARGET FORM: FRETish has one response form (satisfy BEXP), so template wrapper words have no slot; the loss is recorded (unmapped_content)

R-COMP.quote: ID is an identifier starting with an upper- or lower-case letter, followed by letters, digits or underscores
R-COMP.documents: CONSTRUCT (identifier shape); snake_case of the subject words is mechanical

R-SP-COMP.documents: FORCED BY THE TARGET FORM: the component field is mandatory and SPIDER has no subject, so a content-free identifier is required

R-SP-NOMAP.documents: REFUSAL: no FRETish construct is documented for chain, bounded existence, maximum duration, periodic recurrence; the tool produces no sentence (failure recorded, free path)
